rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf omits the object of denial as it had done nearby; Jonah states it explicitly because its preceding passage had named the objects, and each ending suits its context.
rows.anchor: وجاء هنا بما كذبوا فحذف متعلق التكذيب لما حذف المتعلق في ولو أن أهل القرى آمنوا

words: كذلك يطبع الله على قلوب الكافرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with earlier towns, whose capacity for faith vanished and whose disbelief persisted before and after miracles, God seals the hearts of later unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي مثل ذلك الطبع على قلوب أهل القرى حين انتفت عنهم قابلية الإيمان وتساوى أمرهم في الكفر قبل المعجزات وبعدها

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī explains that the verse first refers to God explicitly and by pronoun, then closes with an explicit mention; Jonah instead follows its preceding first-person-plural verbs.
rows.anchor: قال الكرماني تقدم ذكر الله بالصريح وبالكناية فجمع بينهما فقال ونطبع على قلوبهم وختم بالصريح فقال كذلك يطبع الله

rows.speaker: التبريزي
rows.claim: Al-Tabrīzī gives three possible referents for “most of them”: most people, the people of the towns, or earlier nations.
rows.anchor: أي لأكثر الناس أو أهل القرى أو الأمم الماضية احتمالات ثلاثة قاله التبريزي

rows.speaker: أبي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ubayy and Ibn ʿAbbās identify the covenant as the covenant made with humankind in Adam’s loins.
rows.anchor: والعهد هنا هو الذي عوهدوا عليه في صلب آدم قاله أبي وابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd takes the covenant to mean faith, understood as affirming that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: أو الإيمان قاله ابن مسعود ويدل عليه إلا من اتخذ عند الله عهدا وهو لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes the covenant the proofs for God’s oneness and prophethood, binding rational people as contracts do; failure to find it means they did not direct their minds to those proofs.
rows.anchor: وقيل العهد هو وضع الأدلة على صحة التوحيد والنبوة إذ ذلك عهد في رقاب العقلاء كالعقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min is extra here and marks the covenant as exhaustive of its kind.
rows.anchor: ومن في من عهد زائدة تدل على الاستغراق لجنس العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In is the lightened form of emphatic inna, wajadnā means “knew,” the two objects are “most of them” and “fiscally disobedient,” and the lām distinguishes it from negative in.
rows.anchor: إن هنا هي المخففة من الثقيلة ووجد بمعنى علم ومفعول وجدنا الأولى لأكثرهم ومفعول الثانية لفاسقين واللام للفرق بين إن المخففة من الثقيلة وإن النافية

rows.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
rows.claim: Some Kūfan grammarians analyze in here as a negation and the lām as meaning “except.”
rows.anchor: ودعوى بعض الكوفيين أن إن في نحو هذا التركيب هي النافية واللام بمعنى إلا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies an omitted subject, “the matter,” for in; Abū Ḥayyān says that such a supplement is unnecessary and rejects his general account of lightened in.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وإن الشأن والحديث وجدنا انتهى، ولا يحتاج إلى هذا التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the accounts of Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Lot, and Shuʿayb and the destruction of their peoples, the narrative turns to Moses, whose major miracles and people’s persistent denial offer a lesson; some of his followers remained.
rows.anchor: وكان هؤلاء لم يبق منهم أحد أتبع بقصص موسى وفرعون وبني إسرائيل إذ كانت معجزاته من أعظم المعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s story connects to Shuʿayb through their marriage connection and shared descent from Abraham; the plural “We sent” also continues the form used to open Noah’s story.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أن بين موسى وشعيب عليها السلام مصاهرة كما حكى الله في كتابه ونسب لكونهما من نسل إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “after them” may refer to the messengers mentioned earlier or to the preceding communities.
rows.anchor: والضمير في من بعدهم عائد على الرسل من قوله ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات أو للأمم السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs given to Moses are variously identified as proofs against his people, the nine signs, or the Torah.
rows.anchor: والآيات الحجج التي آتاه الله على قومه أو الآيات التسع أو التوراة أقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ can make the phrase mean that they disbelieved the signs, through semantic inclusion of that meaning.
rows.anchor: وتعدية فظلموا بالباء إما على سبيل التضمين بمعنى كفروا بها ألا ترى إلى قوله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the bāʾ is causal: they wronged themselves, people by blocking their faith, or Moses by calling his message magic and deception.
rows.anchor: وإما أن تكون الباء سببية أي ظلموا أنفسهم بسببها أو الناس حيث صدوهم عن الإيمان أو الرسول فقالوا سحر وتمويه

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm says they wronged God’s gifts by using them to disobey Him.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم: ظلموا تلك النعم التي آتاهم الله بأن استعانوا بها على معصية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to look addresses any hearer, presenting the fate of earlier wrongdoers as a warning to the Prophet’s contemporary unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فانظر أيها السامع ما آل إليه أمر المفسدين الظالمين جعلهم مثالا توعد به كفرة عصر الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addresses Pharaoh in the form of address he would most like; “Pharaoh” is a ruler’s title like Caesar or Khosrow, not an individual proper name.
rows.anchor: وخطاب له بأحسن ما يدعى به وأحبها إليه إذ كان من ملك مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Pharaoh claimed divinity, Moses begins by naming the Lord of all worlds, exposing Pharaoh’s false claim to that status.
rows.anchor: ولما كان فرعون قد ادعى الربوبية فاتحه موسى بقوله: إني رسول من رب العالمين

words: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses follows his claim to be a messenger with his commitment to truth, then adduces the clear sign and derives the demand to release Israel.
rows.anchor: ولما كان قوله حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق أردفها بما يدل على صحتها وهو قوله قد جئتكم

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads ʿalayya with a doubled yāʾ, taking ʿalā as attached to the speaker’s pronoun; ḥaqīq means worthy or fitting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع على أن لا أقول بتشديد الياء جعل على داخلة على ياء المتكلم ومعنى حقيق جدير وخليق

words: أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Nāfiʿ’s reading, “not to speak” is best parsed as the subject of ḥaqīq, though it may instead be a subject with ḥaqīq as predicate; another group pauses after ḥaqīq.
rows.anchor: وأن لا أقول الأحسن فيه أن يكون فاعلا بحقيق كأنه قيل يحق علي كذا ويجب

words: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of the seven read ʿalayya with a kasra; this is explained by construing ḥaqīq with the sense “eager.”
rows.anchor: فقال قوم: ضمن حقيق معنى حريص

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن والفراء والفارسي
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan, al-Farrāʾ, and al-Fārisī allow ʿalā to mean bi-, as bi- can mean ʿalā; Abū’s reading with bi- supports this construction.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن والفراء والفارسي: علي بمعنى الباء كما أن الباء بمعنى على في قوله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash objects that substituting ʿalā for bi- is not a general rule: one cannot say “I went ʿalā Zayd” intending “by Zayd.”
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: وليس ذلك بالمطرد لو قلت ذهبت على زيد تريد بزيد لم يجز

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s first solution treats the wording as inverted speech, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects inversion in eloquent Qurʾānic language and restricts it to poetry.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون مما يقلب من الكلام لا من الإلباس كقوله: وتشقى الرماح بالضياطرة الحمر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s second proposal is that the obligation to tell the truth binds Moses because truth-telling is incumbent on him.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن ما لزمك لزمته فلما كان قول الحق حقيقا عليه كان هو حقيقا على قول الحق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s third proposal gives ḥaqīq the sense “eager,” by analogy with a line where hayyajanī means “reminded” or “stirred me.”
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والثالث أن يضمن حقيق معنى حريص

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the emphatic self-description the strongest proposal: Moses insists he alone is bound to speak truth, especially given the report that Pharaoh called him a liar.
rows.anchor: والرابع وهو الأوجه وإلا دخل في نكت القرآن أن يغرق موسى عليه السلام في وصف نفسه بالصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Zamakhsharī’s preferred explanation works only if the following phrase describes Moses’s path or habit of truth-telling.
rows.anchor: ولا يتضح هذا الوجه إلا إن عنى أنه يكون على أن لا أقول صفة كما تقول أنا على قول الحق

rows.speaker: ابن مقسم
rows.claim: Ibn Miqsam attaches ʿalā to the sense of “messenger,” understanding Moses as sent to speak only truth; Abū Ḥayyān finds this clear in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مقسم حقيق من نعت الرسول أي رسول حقيق من رب العالمين أرسلت على أن لا أقول

words: حقيق على أن لا أقول على الله إلا الحق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn Miqsam’s explanation appears contradictory: he first posits an implied “I was sent,” then says others failed to attach ʿalā to messenger; understood as attachment to the meaning of messenger, the first estimate is sound, though direct attachment violates Basran grammar.
rows.anchor: الأول وهو إضمار أرسلت ويفسره لفظ رسول فهو تقدير سائغ

rows.speaker: عبد الله والأعمش
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh and al-Aʿmash omit ʿalā; one may supply it implicitly or supply bi- as in Abū’s reading, and either construction attaches to ḥaqīq.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والأعمش حقيق أن لا أقول بإسقاط على فاحتمل أن يكون على إضمار على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing his mission and truthfulness, Moses now adduces the extraordinary sign that proves the message.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر أنه رسول من عند الله وأنه لا يقول على الله إلا الحق أخذ يذكر المعجزة والخارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address “I have brought you” is to Pharaoh and the chiefs present; bayyina means a clear sign whose proof supports Moses’s assertion.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في جئتكم لفرعون وملائه الحاضرين معه ومعنى ببينة بآية بينة واضحة الدلالة على ما أذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the sign as all nine signs mentioned in the other passage.
rows.anchor: البينة قيل: التسع الآيات المذكورة في قوله في تسع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars say the context requires the staff and white hand; Ibn ʿAbbās and most commentators identify the sign as the staff.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والأكثرون هي العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From your Lord” implies that Pharaoh is not their lord; their true Lord sent Moses with the sign.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله من ربكم تعريض أن فرعون ليس ربا لهم بل ربهم هو الذي جاء موسى بالبينة من عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-arsil means “release” or “let go,” the opposite of retaining; Moses asks Pharaoh to let Israel return to their homeland, the Holy Land where their fathers were born.
rows.anchor: فأرسل أي فخل والإرسال ضد الإمساك معي بني إسرائيل أي حتى يذهبوا إلى أوطانهم ومولد آبائهم الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Joseph died and the tribes disappeared, Pharaoh subdued their descendants, enslaved them in hard labor, and imposed tribute; Moses rescued them, four hundred years after Joseph entered Egypt.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن يوسف عليه السلام لما توفي وانقرض الأسباط غلب فرعون على نسلهم واستعبدهم في الأعمال الشاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this passage explicitly asks only for Israel’s release, Moses elsewhere calls Pharaoh to purify himself and fear God, and Pharaoh’s own words confirm that Moses demanded belief; this rebuts those who deny he invited faith or commitment to the law.
rows.anchor: وفي غير هذه الآية دعاؤه إياه إلى الإقرار بربوبية الله تعالى وتوحيده قال تعالى فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelites are not Pharaoh’s people or the Copts: most of the remaining Copts did not follow Moses.
rows.anchor: وليس بنو إسرائيل من قوم فرعون والقبط ألا ترى أن بقية القبط وهم الأكثر لم يرجع إليهم موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for additional staff miracles: striking a rock to release springs and striking the ground so plants grew; other reports describe its practical uses and its defeat of sorcery.
rows.anchor: وضربه بها الحجر فينفجر عيونا وضربه بها فتنبت قاله ابن عباس ومحاربته بها اللصوص والسباع القاصدة غنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transformation from wood into living flesh and blood and the serpent’s terrifying appearance are further aspects of the miracle.
rows.anchor: وانقلاب خشبة لحما ودما قائما به الحياة من أعظم الإعجاز ويحصل من انقلابها ثعبانا من التهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “cast” is literal for physical objects but metaphorical for meanings, as in casting a question.
rows.anchor: والإلقاء حقيقة هو في الأجرام ومجاز في المعاني نحو ألقى المسألة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad calls idhā a locative adverb because it is a predicate of a concrete entity; Abū Ḥayyān disputes that explanation in this construction.
rows.anchor: فإذا ظرف مكان في هذا الموضع عند المبرد من حيث كانت خبرا عن جثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are the intelligent nobles at Pharaoh’s council; they advised delay instead of execution because killing Moses could make people suspect he was truthful.
rows.anchor: أي قال من حضر مناظرة موسى من عقلاء ملأ فرعون وأشرافه قيل: ولم يكن يجالس فرعون ولد غية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unhamzated form is variously treated as equivalent to the hamzated form, as “detain him,” or as “make him hopeful” from rajā; Moses and Aaron are to be held until their claim is exposed.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالهمز وبغير همز فقيل هما بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron has not yet been mentioned in this account, but other verses establish that the two went together; the advisers include him because he supports Moses’s claim.
rows.anchor: ولم يجر لهارون ذكر في صدر القصة وقد تبين من غير آية أنهما ذهبا معا وأرسلا إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse has numerous transmitted forms varying in hamza, the vowel of hāʾ, and whether hāʾ is linked by wāw or yāʾ; Abū Ḥayyān catalogs their attribution to the readers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وهشام أرجئهو بالهمز وضم الهاء ووصلها بواو

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes the hamzated form with kasra to Ibn ʿĀmir; Abū Ḥayyān says the attribution should specify Ibn Dhakwān’s transmission, not Ibn ʿĀmir generally.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية وقرأ ابن عامر أرجئه بكسر الهاء بهمزة قبلها، قال الفارسي

rows.speaker: الفارسي وأبو علي وابن مجاهد والحوفي وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: Several grammarians call kasra after hamza erroneous or weak because the preceding hamza is a consonant, though they propose vowel assimilation or treating hamza as a replaceable weak letter.
rows.anchor: وما ذهب إليه الفارسي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that criticism: the reading is mutawātir, accepted by the community, and has a grammatical explanation; hamza can undergo substitution and other changes unlike ordinary consonants.
rows.anchor: ولها توجيه في العربية وليست الهمزة كغيرها من الحروف الصحيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cities are the towns and cities of Egypt.
rows.anchor: المدائن مدائن مصر وقراها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the gatherers as police officers.
rows.anchor: والحاشرون، قال ابن عباس هم أصحاب الشرط

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Pharaoh concluded that only someone like Moses could match him and therefore recruited young men; the excerpt breaks off after this statement begins.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق لما رأى فرعون من آيات الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shows that magic does not physically transform the eyes; its effect is illusion.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله سحروا أعين الناس دلالة على أن السحر لا يقلب عينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istarhabūhum means “frightened them”; here the istifʿāl form equals ifʿāl, since seeking fear would not itself prove that fear occurred.
rows.anchor: واسترهبوهم أي أرهبوهم واستفعل هنا بمعنى أفعل كأبل واستبل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya instead explain the form as soliciting or eliciting fear; Abū Ḥayyān says seeking does not guarantee the result, whereas the verse shows fear occurred.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: واسترهبوهم وأرهبوهم إرهابا شديدا كأنهم استدعوا رهبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their magic is called great because the illusion was powerful or because the ropes and sticks were numerous.
rows.anchor: ووصف السحر بعظيم لقوة ما خيل أو لكثرة آلاته من الحبال والعصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says the magicians used leather ropes and hollow wooden sticks filled with quicksilver, heated by fire below and sun above so they moved like snakes; Abū Ḥayyān calls this sleight of hand.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم جاؤوا بحبال من أدم وأخشاب مجوفة مملوءة زيبقا وأوقدوا في الوادي نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text elides “he said, ‘Throw,’ then they threw”; the fāʾ links to that deleted statement, rather than directly answering the command as al-Ḥawfī proposes.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره قال ألقوا فألقوا فلما ألقوا والفاء عاطفة على هذا المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magic is “great” for its effects on visible eyes and inward hearts, and the sentence about terror follows because fear arose from what eyes saw.
rows.anchor: وصف بعظيم لما ظهر من تأثيره في الأعضاء الظاهرة التي هي الأعين

words: وإذ قالت أمة منهم لم تعظون قوما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading has three groups: transgressors, preachers, and a third group that neither sinned nor admonished; the questioners are distinct from those addressed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن القائل غير المقول لهم لم تعظون قوما فيكون ثلاث فرق اعتدوا وفرقة وعظت ونهت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative report has only two groups: sinners and admonishers, with some sinners mockingly asking why they preach to people God will destroy or punish.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم كانوا فرقتين فرقة عصت وفرقة نهت ووعظت وأن جماعة من العاصية قالت للواعظة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the three-group account: the direct plural address “your Lord” and “they may fear” implies an audience separate from the questioners.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والقول الأول أصوب ويؤيده الضمائر في قوله معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhlikuhum may mean removing them and purifying the land of them, or punishing them severely for persisting in disobedience; the excerpt begins but does not complete a further qualification about worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: ومعنى مهلكهم مخترمهم ومطهر الأرض منهم أو معذبهم عذابا شديدا لتماديهم في العصيان

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī glosses the prophecy as sending or empowering someone over them, comparing it with the sending of servants against the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الدمشقي أعلم أنبياء بني إسرائيل ليبعثن ليرسلن وليسلطن لقوله بعثنا عليكم عبادا لنا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the pronoun “against them” to refer to the Jews.
rows.anchor: والضمير في عليهم عائد على اليهود قاله الجمهور

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid takes the pronoun to refer to both Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: أو عليهم وعلى النصارى قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed referents are the descendants of those transformed into apes and those who remained, or the Jews of Khaybar, Qurayẓa, and Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نسل الممسوخين والذين بقوا منهم وقيل: يهود خيبر وقريظة والنضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proposed agents of the humiliation include Nebuchadnezzar and later rulers, the Magians, Arabs collecting tax, or Muhammad and his community; Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses alone among prophets collected tribute, for thirteen years.
rows.anchor: ومن أذلهم بعده إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the Arabs collected tax from the Jews.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العرب كانوا يجبون الخراج من اليهود قاله ابن جبير

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God sent Arabs against the Jews to collect jizya and kill them.
rows.anchor: السدي بعث الله عليهم العرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the agents as Muḥammad and his community, adding that no prophet collected jizya except Moses, who did so for thirteen years before it ceased for Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس المبعوث عليهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته ولم يجب الخراج نبي قط إلا موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the severe punishment as jizya, or jizya together with poverty and humiliation; another view is fighting until submission or payment of jizya in abasement.
rows.anchor: وسوء العذاب الجزية أو الجزية والمسكنة وكلاهما عن ابن عباس أو القتال حتى يسلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is expulsion from the homeland, if the pronoun refers to the Jews of Khaybar, Qurayẓa, and Naḍīr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإخراج والإبعاد عن الوطن وذلك على قول من قال إن الضمير في عليهم عائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reads the prophecy as denying the Jews lasting sovereignty or honor; its fulfillment in the Prophet’s time and thereafter is a truthful report of the unseen and thus a miracle.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أن لا دولة لليهود ولا عز وأن الذل والصغار فيهم لا يفارقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report that the Dajjāl’s followers are Jews is sound, it names them by their former identity, since at that time they follow the Dajjāl’s claim to divinity; it does not conflict with the verse.
rows.anchor: وأما ما جاء في أتباع الدجال أنهم هم اليهود فتسمية بما كانوا عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s book recounts that impoverished Romans in one district sold neighboring Jews and took ownership of them.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب ابن عطية: ولقد حدثت أن طائفة من الروم أملقت في صقعها فباعت اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about swift punishment implies that God brings punishment on them quickly.
rows.anchor: إن ربك لسريع العقاب. إخبار يتضمن سرعة إيقاع العذاب بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of forgiveness gives hope to those who believe and to anyone who repents and reforms.
rows.anchor: وإنه لغفور رحيم. ترجية لمن آمن منهم ومن غيرهم ووعد لمن تاب وأصلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites were scattered into separate groups across the earth; every land has some of them, living under humiliation under Muslim or non-Muslim rulers.
rows.anchor: أي فرقا متباينين في أقطار الأرض فقل أرض لا يكون منهم فيها شرذمة وهذا حالهم في كل مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān parses umaman as a circumstantial accusative; al-Ḥawfī instead treats it as a second object, and the author notes an earlier discussion of the phrase.
rows.anchor: وأمما حال، وقال الحوفي مفعول ثان وتقدم قوله هذا في قطعناهم اثنتي عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are variously identified as those who believed in Jesus and Muḥammad or as those who believed in Medina.
rows.anchor: والصالحون من آمن منهم بعيسى ومحمد عليهما السلام أو من آمن بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ṣalāḥ means faith, “below that” means unbelievers; if it means worship, goodness, and related traits beyond faith, it can mean believers who have not reached the righteous group’s rank.
rows.anchor: والصالحون ودون ذلك ألفاظ محتملة فإن أريد بالصلاح الإيمان فدون ذلك يراد به الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the first interpretation, where “below that” means unbelievers, because the tested people are those who remained Jews and left faith, whom God hopes will return.
rows.anchor: والظاهر الاحتمال الأول لقوله لعلهم يرجعون إذ ظاهر قوله وبلوناهم أنهم القوم الذين هم دون أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dūn is originally a locative adverb and is extended to express lower rank.
rows.anchor: ودون ذلك ظرف أصله للمكان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says that when righteousness means faith, dūn means “other than,” referring to unbelievers; Abū Ḥayyān rejects treating dūn and ghayr as synonyms but accepts the inference that those below are other than the group.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: فإن أريد بالصلاح الإيمان فدون ذلك بمعنى غير يراد بها الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dūn is a nominative adverb modifying an omitted noun; alternatively, the described noun is omitted and its quality stands in its place, as in “some of us traveled, some stayed.”
rows.anchor: ودون ظرف في موضع رفع نعت لمنعوت محذوف ويجوز في التفصيل بمن حذف الموصوف وإقامة صفته مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings and harms are health, prosperity, and abundance and their opposites.
rows.anchor: أي بالصحة والرخاء والسعة والسيئات مقابلاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trials aim to bring them back to obedience and repentance from sin.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون إلى الطاعة ويتوبون عن المعصية

words: فخلف من بعدهم خلف ورثوا الكتاب
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says khalaf is a generation that comes after another generation.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال للقرن الذي يجيء بعد القرن خلف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says khalaf can mean the succeeding generation, while khulf means the one installed as a successor; elsewhere he associates khalaf with blame and khulf with a righteous successor.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الخلف القرن والخلف من استخلفه

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab reports the common distinction: “good successor” is khulf ṣidq and “bad successor” is khalaf sūʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال ثعلب: الناس كلهم يقولون خلف صدق للصالح وخلف سوء للطالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem uses khalaf negatively for people who remain after those once cherished, likening them to a scabby hide.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: ذهب الذين يعاش في أكنافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proverb “he was silent for a thousand, then spoke a khalaf” uses khalaf for a long-awaited but bad utterance.
rows.anchor: والمثل: سكت ألفا ونطق خلفا أي سكت طويلا ثم تكلم بكلام فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line calls a successor blameworthy, while Ḥassān’s verse is cited for the praiseworthy sense; the latter text is cut off here.
rows.anchor: وفي الصالح خلف وعلى هذا بيت حسان:
